# Park Pane: a pane leaves the split with its program running, and comes
# back where it stood. Read back as the tab's row and the shells' text.
type:echo MAIN-PANE
key:enter
wait:0.5
key:cmd+d
wait:1.0
type:echo PARKED-PANE; sleep 2; echo STILL-RUNNING
key:enter
wait:0.5
expect-tab:2 panes
# Park the focused (new) pane from the palette.
key:cmd+shift+p
wait:0.4
type:park pane
wait:0.3
expect-palette:Park Pane
key:enter
wait:1.0
expect-tab:1 parked
expect-not:2 panes
# Its program ran on while it was away.
wait:2.5
expect:STILL-RUNNING
# Parking the only pane in view is refused: nothing would be left.
key:cmd+shift+p
wait:0.4
type:park pane
wait:0.3
key:enter
wait:0.6
expect-tab:1 parked
# Unpark: back in the split, the same shell.
key:cmd+shift+p
wait:0.4
type:unpark pane
wait:0.3
expect-palette:Unpark Pane
key:enter
wait:1.0
expect-tab:2 panes
expect-not:parked
type:echo BACK-AGAIN
key:enter
wait:0.6
expect:BACK-AGAIN
shot:park.png
# Park pressed twice in a row parks the pane once.
key:cmd+shift+p
wait:0.4
type:park pane
wait:0.3
key:enter
key:cmd+shift+p
wait:0.1
type:park pane
key:enter
wait:1.0
expect-tab:1 parked
expect-not:2 parked
